writeup: TIC 446692149 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 19.4695 days. Analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 6.39 percent, with a detection signal-to-noise ratio of 52.3. Pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal at a peak signal-to-noise of 15.3, though the centroid offset measured 4.7 arcseconds from the target location. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.38 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing system rather than an instrumental artifact or other false positive.
